I work on the service desk.
You meet a colleague from another department for the first time. Tell them that you work on the service desk.
Op de servicedesk identifies your team or workplace, rather than a task you are currently troubleshooting.
I support users with their everyday computer problems.
During an informal introduction, a colleague asks what kind of support you provide. Explain that you help users with everyday computer problems.
Gebruikers is the plural object; hun refers to those users. Bij introduces the situations in which you support them.
My first point of contact is the team leader.
You have just joined the support team. Tell a colleague who your first point of contact is.
Aanspreekpunt is a het-word, but mijn replaces the article. The complete phrase Mijn eerste aanspreekpunt is one subject constituent.
Q=Welke collega's|V=werken|PP=aan dezelfde meldingen als ik?
Which colleagues work on the same support requests as I do?
You are learning how work is shared. Ask which colleagues deal with the same support requests as you.
The question phrase Welke collega's is itself the plural subject. Aan introduces the requests being worked on; als ik completes the comparison.
Are you my mentor on the service desk?
On your first day, you meet a colleague who may be your assigned mentor. Ask them informally whether that is their role.
Ben is the inverted present form before jij. Begeleider means the person guiding your onboarding here.
S=Ons team|V=beheert|O=de computers van de medewerkers.
Our team manages the employees' computers.
A new colleague asks what your team is responsible for. Explain that it manages the employees' computers.
Team is a singular het-word, so use ons team. The employees own/use the computers; they are not the subject managing them.
From Monday onward, I will work with the systems administrators.
You are explaining a confirmed change to your work assignment. Tell a colleague that you will start working with the systems administrators on Monday.
Vanaf means from that time onward. A present verb with a future starting point can describe a confirmed arrangement.
Ik werk vanaf maandag samen met de systeembeheerders.
From Monday onward, I will work with the systems administrators.
The subject moves first and the starting-time phrase follows the finite verb. The arrangement and time remain the same.
I do not know everyone in the support team yet.
A colleague assumes you know the whole support team. Explain that you have not yet become acquainted with every member.
Nog niet iedereen means not everyone yet; it does not mean you know no one. Kennen concerns familiarity with people.
I met my new colleagues yesterday.
A colleague asks about yesterday's onboarding. Say that you met your new colleagues then.
Nieuwe identifies recently joined colleagues in this context. Heb ontmoet reports the completed meeting; it does not claim you already know them well.
I would like to introduce myself to the support team.
You are attending the support team's meeting for the first time. Politely indicate that you would like to introduce yourself to the group.
Stel me voor is reflexive and separable. Graag softens your introduction; it does not claim that you have already introduced yourself.
Where can I find the workstations for the support team?
You are new in the building. Ask a colleague where the support team's workstations are located.
Waar asks for location. Vind before subject ik is the ordinary ik form; no extra kan is required in Dutch.
Is this meeting room available for a support call?
You need a room for a support call. Ask a colleague whether this meeting room is available for that purpose.
Vrij means unoccupied/available in this context, not free of charge. Voor names its intended use.
A user's keyboard needs replacing. Ask your colleague where the spare keyboard is kept.
Het reservetoetsenbord is the subject. Staan is a natural location verb for equipment kept ready for use.
May I use this shared workstation today?
You see a shared workstation and want to use it today. Ask a colleague for permission rather than assuming it is assigned to you.
Werkplek is a de-word: deze gedeelde werkplek. Mag asks permission; physical availability alone does not establish it.
Which entrance do we use outside office hours?
You may need to enter the building for scheduled work outside office hours. Ask a colleague which entrance the team uses then.
Welke ingang is the object question phrase, while we is the subject. Buiten de kantooruren is common Belgian phrasing for outside office hours.
There is a quiet room for confidential conversations.
A colleague needs privacy for a confidential conversation. Explain that a quiet room is available for that purpose.
Er introduces the existence of een stille ruimte. The room is grammatically the singular subject, despite appearing after is.
MOD=Kun|S=je|O=me|I=tonen|G=waar het materiaal voor nieuwe medewerkers ligt?
Can you show me where the equipment for new employees is?
You need equipment for a new employee but do not know where it is stored. Ask a colleague informally to show you.
Me is the person to be shown. The embedded location question ends in ligt; materiaal is an uncountable het-word.
L=Naast de receptie|V=ligt|S=de lijst met interne telefoonnummers.
The list of internal telephone numbers is next to reception.
A new colleague asks for internal phone numbers. Tell them where the physical list is located.
The whole location phrase is first. Ligt suits a list lying on a surface; de lijst is the subject.
De lijst met interne telefoonnummers ligt naast de receptie.
The list of internal telephone numbers is next to reception.
Putting the list first restores subject–verb order; its location and meaning remain the same.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=de werkplek voor de nieuwe medewerker|PT=klaargemaakt.
I have prepared the workstation for the new employee.
Your team leader asks about the incoming employee's workstation. Report that you have finished preparing it.
Klaargemaakt is a separable participle. The completed preparation does not claim that the employee has already arrived.
S=Ik|V=weet|NEG=nog niet|G=waar we defect materiaal bewaren.
I do not yet know where we keep faulty equipment.
A colleague asks you to put faulty equipment away. Explain that you do not yet know the designated storage location.
Waar introduces an embedded location question with final bewaren. Defect materiaal is faulty equipment, not a diagnosis of its cause.
I am the first point of contact for users this morning.
Your team is confirming today's coverage. Tell a colleague that you are the first person users should contact this morning.
Vanochtend limits the assignment to this morning. Aanspreekpunt refers to a contact role, not a physical desk.
T=Na twee uur|V=heb|S=ik|O=tijd voor nieuwe meldingen.
After two o'clock, I have time for new support requests.
A colleague asks when you can handle additional requests today. Say that you have time for them after two o'clock.
Na twee uur means after two o'clock in this schedule context, not after a two-hour duration.
Ik heb na twee uur tijd voor nieuwe meldingen.
After two o'clock, I have time for new support requests.
The subject comes first and the same time phrase follows heb; the availability remains after two o'clock.
I am not reachable by phone during the training.
You are about to attend training. Tell your team that phone calls will not reach you during that period.
Niet negates telephone reachability. The sentence does not rule out every other contact channel.
Can you support the service desk until I return?
You must step away temporarily. Ask a colleague informally to support the service desk until you return.
Tot mijn terugkomst gives an ending condition for the requested support, not a permanent reassignment.
Are you available tomorrow between nine and ten?
You are arranging a support appointment with a customer you address formally. Ask whether tomorrow between nine and ten is available.
Formal u keeps bent in inversion. Tussen ... en defines one time window; it is not a choice between two appointments.
I have put my working hours in the shared calendar.
A colleague asks where to check your availability. Explain that you have entered your working hours in the shared calendar.
Agenda means a calendar here, not the meeting's list of topics. Gezet is the irregular participle of zetten.
I will let you know if my availability changes.
You have just agreed on your availability with a colleague. Promise to notify them if that availability changes.
Het refers to the update and je is the receiver. Als introduces a condition; this does not predict that the schedule will change.
This morning I was briefly away from my desk.
A colleague tried to reach you earlier this morning. Explain that you were briefly away from your desk then.
Was reports a past state. Even limits the absence to a short period rather than the whole morning.
T=Deze week|V=heb|S=ik|O=minder tijd voor extra taken dan vorige week.
This week I have less time for extra tasks than last week.
A colleague asks you to take on additional work. Explain that you have less spare task time this week than you did last week.
Minder tijd compares an uncountable amount; dan introduces the comparison. Deze week is a time phrase, not the grammatical subject.
S=Ik|MOD=zal|O=mijn overdracht|PP=voor het einde van mijn dienst|I=voorbereiden.
I will prepare my handover before the end of my shift.
Your colleague will take over after your shift. Promise to prepare the handover before your shift ends.
Voor het einde sets a deadline. Voorbereiden remains joined after zal; the sentence is a commitment, not a completion report.
When can we arrange our breaks?
The support team needs continuous coverage. Ask a colleague when you can agree how to stagger your breaks.
Onze refers to plural pauzes. Verdelen means distribute/arrange them across the group here, not take all breaks at once.
I will take my lunch break after the user appointment.
A teammate asks about your lunch plans. Explain that your lunch break will follow the appointment with a user.
The present expresses an arranged sequence in this context. It does not imply that the user appointment is already finished.
Can you include the new colleague at lunch?
A newcomer is joining the team today. Ask another colleague informally to include that person when the group has lunch.
Betrekken bij means include in. The new colleague receives inclusion rather than an assigned support task.
I have not taken a break since the first phone call.
A teammate asks whether you have rested during the busy shift. Explain that you have not taken a break since the first call.
Heb ... genomen is the perfect of nemen. Nog geen means not any break yet; sinds identifies the starting point of that period.
I will return as soon as my break is over.
Before taking your break, tell the colleague covering you that you will return as soon as it ends.
Zodra gives a future time condition with final is. The main present kom can express the promised return.
We do not discuss confidential user details during the lunch break.
You are explaining a team privacy practice to a colleague. Say that confidential user details are not discussed over lunch.
Geen negates the plural indefinite gegevens. This describes a privacy practice, not a refusal to discuss all work topics.
We bespreken tijdens de middagpauze geen vertrouwelijke gebruikersgegevens.
We do not discuss confidential user details during the lunch break.
The subject starts the sentence while the lunch-break time phrase moves inside it; the privacy practice is unchanged.
T=Gisteren|PAST=bleef|S=ik|T=tijdens de pauze|C=bij de nieuwe medewerker.
Yesterday I stayed with the new employee during the break.
A colleague asks how you helped the new employee settle in yesterday. Say that you stayed with them during the break.
Bleef is singular past of blijven. Bij describes being with the employee, not working on a support ticket.
Let's take our break in turns.
You and a colleague both need a break while support coverage must continue. Suggest taking the break in turns.
Om beurten is a fixed expression meaning in turns. It is not an om te infinitive phrase.
Is there still room at your lunch table?
You would like to join colleagues for lunch. Ask informally whether there is still room at their table.
Existential er introduces available room. Nog means still; jullie is a plural possessive referring to the colleagues.
S=Ik|V=gebruik|O=de pauze|TE=om even weg van het scherm te zijn.
I use the break to spend a little time away from the screen.
A colleague asks why you step away from your computer during breaks. Explain that you use the break to spend a short time away from the screen.
Om te zijn names the purpose; even means briefly. It does not say that you leave the building.
I have experience with remote user support.
A colleague asks about your previous support experience. Explain that you have worked with remote user support.
Ervaring met is a fixed combination. This is a present statement of experience, not an assertion that every remote problem is familiar.
I want to get to know the internal applications better.
You are discussing your learning goals with a teammate. Say that you want to become more familiar with the internal applications.
Leren kennen describes gaining familiarity. Wanting to learn is not the same as already knowing how each application works.
I am not familiar with this procedure from my previous role.
A colleague asks whether a procedure is familiar from your earlier job. Explain that you did not encounter it in that role.
Kennen uit names the source of familiarity. Vorige means previous, not necessarily a different employer.
I still feel uncertain when dealing with complex disruptions.
Your mentor asks where you need support. Explain that complex disruptions still make you feel unsure.
Voel me describes your feeling; gevoel would be a noun. Nog signals that this uncertainty continues for now.
I feel positive about this task.
A colleague asks how you feel about an assigned task. Explain that your overall feeling about it is positive.
Gevoel is a noun inside the subject Mijn gevoel bij deze taak. It is not the finite verb voel.
I have previously worked with a similar ticketing system.
You are learning the team's request system. Explain to your mentor that you have worked with a similar system before.
Soortgelijk means similar, not identical. The perfect reports experience without claiming mastery of the current system.
Which skills do I especially need for this role?
You are planning how to develop in your new role. Ask your manager which skills are particularly important for it.
Welke vaardigheden is the object question phrase. Heb ... nodig is the need construction; vooral asks about emphasis.
S=Ik|V=weet|G=dat ik nog veel over ons netwerk moet leren.
I know that I still have a lot to learn about our network.
During a learning review, acknowledge to your mentor that there is still a lot you need to learn about the team's network.
Dat introduces known content. Ons belongs with singular het netwerk; moet leren is a final verb group.
Can I carry out this task with you first?
You are about to perform an unfamiliar task. Ask your colleague informally whether you can do it together the first time.
Samen met jou identifies collaboration, not handing the task over entirely. Eerst places the joint attempt before independent work.
S=Ik|V=maak|O=aantekeningen|TE=om de stappen later zelfstandig te herhalen.
I take notes so I can repeat the steps independently later.
A colleague is demonstrating a task to you. Explain that you are taking notes so that you can repeat the steps on your own later.
The om te phrase expresses a learning purpose. Later distinguishes independent repetition from the current demonstration.
S=Ik|V=werk|T=twee dagen per week|L=van thuis uit.
I work from home two days a week.
A colleague asks about your regular work arrangement. Explain that you work from home two days each week.
Van thuis uit is standard Belgian wording for working from home. The sentence states frequency without naming the days.
On my work-from-home day, I am reachable through the same chat group.
A teammate asks how to contact you while you work from home. Say that the same chat group can be used on that day.
The complete day phrase is first, so ben precedes ik. Dezelfde means the same rather than merely a similar group.
Ik ben op mijn thuiswerkdag via dezelfde chatgroep bereikbaar.
On my work-from-home day, I am reachable through the same chat group.
Putting ik first changes the word order but keeps the day and contact channel unchanged.
S=Ik|V=kom|T=morgen|L=naar kantoor|G=omdat de nieuwe medewerker begeleiding nodig heeft.
I am coming to the office tomorrow because the new employee needs guidance.
Your colleague asks why you will be in the office tomorrow. Explain that the new employee needs guidance there.
Omdat gives a reason, not a condition. Nodig heeft closes the subordinate clause; tomorrow's visit is an arrangement.
I cannot be reached on the internal extension at home.
A colleague tries to use your internal extension while you work remotely. Explain that this number does not reach you at home.
Niet negates reachability through that specific number. It does not say that every contact method is unavailable.
Can we do the handover through a video call?
You and a colleague will be in different locations at shift change. Ask whether the handover can take place through a video call.
Kunnen expresses a proposed practical option. The question does not claim that a handover has already taken place.
I have agreed my work-from-home day with the team leader.
A colleague asks whether your remote-work arrangement has been coordinated. Say that you have agreed the day with the team leader.
Afgestemd is the separable participle. Met identifies the person consulted; the statement concerns an agreed arrangement.
I am getting my home workstation ready.
Before starting a remote shift, a colleague asks what you are doing now. Explain that you are currently preparing your home workstation.
Aan het klaarmaken describes preparation in progress. It does not imply the workstation is already ready.
Which tasks can we carry out just as well remotely?
Your team is comparing remote and office work. Ask which tasks can be carried out equally well remotely.
Even goed means equally well, not briefly well. The question concerns practical suitability, not blanket permission.
T=Tijdens mijn vorige thuiswerkdag|PAST=had|S=ik|O=regelmatig contact met de servicedesk.
During my previous work-from-home day, I had regular contact with the service desk.
Your manager asks about communication on your previous remote-working day. Report that you were in regular contact with the service desk.
Had is singular past. Regelmatig means regularly; it does not mean continuously or on one specific channel.
G=Als ik van locatie verander,|V=werk|S=ik|O=mijn bereikbaarheid in de agenda|PART=bij.
When I change location, I update my contact availability in the calendar.
A teammate asks how they can find your current availability. Explain the routine you follow whenever you change work location.
The whole als-clause is the first constituent; werk follows before ik. Bijwerken splits as werk ... bij in the main clause.
